---
title: "Walkshed Routing"
params:
  city: ""
---

Estimated time to run: Several hours (experimenter's PC took 30 hours to route walksheds for New York, the heaviest (in terms of tracts) city in the experiment, but many other cities take only a few hours).

A [walkshed](https://pedshed.net/?page_id=5), also called a pedestrian shed, is the measure of how far a person can walk starting at a given location within a given time range (in this project, within 15 minutes). This is heavily dependent on street layouts.

Load packages:
```{r}
options(java.parameters = "-Xmx20G")
library(dplyr) # A Grammar of Data Manipulation
library(ggraph) # An Implementation of Grammar of Graphics for Graphs and Networks
library(ggplot2) # Create Elegant Data Visualisations Using the Grammar of Graphics
library(ggspatial)
library(glue) # Interpreted String Literals
library(here) # A Simpler Way to Find Your Files
library(igraph) # Network Analysis and Visualization
library(sf) # Simple Features for R
library(sfnetworks) # Tidy Geospatial Networks
library(tidygraph) # A Tidy API for Graph Manipulation
library(tidyr) # Tidy Messy Data
library(r5r) # Rapid Realistic Routing with 'R5'
library(h3) # R Bindings for H3 # R Bindings for H3
# 'remotes::install_github("crazycapivara/h3-r")' for the h3 package
library(purrr) # Functional Programming Tools
library(units) # Measurement Units for R Vectors
```

## Setting up the Data:

Load data:
```{r load files part 1}
# Tracts
load(file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data-raw/intermediate-data-objects/{params$city}_tracts_df.rda"))

# CBSA boundary
load(file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data-raw/intermediate-data-objects/{params$city}_cbsa.rda"))

# cbsa <- merged_cbsa_urban
```

## Network data

Retrieve OSM data from [BBBike](https://extract.bbbike.org) using the coordinates of the bounding box found in `/notebooks/00-Basic-Data.Rmd`. It will be a proto-buffer file (pbf). Save under `data-raw/r5_graph/$CITY_NAME$`. This has to be done manually before running the remainder of this notebook.

Then, set up the pathing to the PBF file to use for the {r5r} routing:
```{r set up r5 path}
r5_path <- file.path(glue::glue(here::here(), "/data-raw/r5_graph/{params$city}/"))
# fix pathing when possible
```

Build the network graph:
```{r r build-graph}
r5_cma <- setup_r5(data_path = r5_path, 
                            verbose = FALSE)

# requires JDK version 21 (exactly version 21) to run

# in newer r5r versions, may not work. In that case, use:
# r5_cma <- r5r::build_network(data_path = r5_path, 
#                             verbose = FALSE)
```

Rename the imported/reopened files:
```{r}
tracts <- urban_tracts_df

cbsa <- merged_cbsa_urban
```

The origins are coordinates of centroids tracts and the destinations the coordinates of the h3 geohashes. 

Obtain the tract centroids (the geometry is degenerate and needs to be fixed):
```{r prepare-inputs}
origins_da <- tracts |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_centroid() |>
  # Transform to lat-long
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(4326))
```

Organize the data for the origins to match the format expected by {r5r} (id, lon, lat):
```{r}
origins_i_tract <- data.frame(id = tracts$GEOID,
                           origins_da |>
                          st_coordinates()) |>
  rename(lon = X, lat = Y) |>
  dplyr::select(id, lon, lat)
```

This is the maximum area with a walking speed of 5.0 km/h and a time of 15 min:
```{r}
pi * (units::set_units(3.6, km/h) |> set_units(m/min) * set_units(15, min))^2
```

Obtain an h3 that covers a larger area:
```{r}
h3_i <- geo_to_h3(c(origins_i_tract$lat[1], origins_i_tract$lon[1]), res = 8) |>
  k_ring(1) |> h3_set_to_multi_polygon()

h3_i |> st_area()
```

Obtain the children of the chosen polygon(s):
```{r}
i <- 1
h3_i <- geo_to_h3(c(origins_i_tract$lat[i], origins_i_tract$lon[i]), res = 7) |>
  k_ring(1)

h3_j <- purrr::map(h3_i,
                   .f = ~ h3_to_children(.x,
                                  res = 13)) |>
  unlist()
```

Check coverage of the children (make sure that the parents are fully covered):
```{r}
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = h3_i |> h3_set_to_multi_polygon()) + 
  geom_sf(data = h3_to_geo_boundary_sf(h3_j), fill = NA)
```

Obtain the coordinates of the h3 destinations:
```{r set destinations}
destinations_h3 <- h3_to_geo(h3_j)
```

Likewise, organize the data for the origins to match the format expected by {r5r} (id, lon, lat):
```{r set destination sites}
destinations_j_h3 <- data.frame(id = h3_j, 
                             lat = destinations_h3[,1],
                             lon = destinations_h3[,2])
```

Test routing with a single origin:
```{r routing test}
ttm_test <- travel_time_matrix(r5_cma,
                                  origins = origins_i_tract[i,],
                                  destinations = destinations_j_h3,
                                  mode = "WALK",
                                  departure_datetime = as.POSIXct(strptime("2021-04-05 08:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "EST5EDT")),
                                  max_walk_time = 15, # minutes
                                  max_trip_duration = 15)

ttm_test <- ttm_test |>
  rename(from_id = to_id,
         to_id = from_id)
```

Retrieve the walkshed as a multipolygon:
```{r walkshed multipolygon test}
walkshed_test <- h3_set_to_multi_polygon(ttm_test$to_id) |> 
  as_tibble() |> st_as_sf(crs = 4326)
```

Compare the walkshed to the parent h3s:
```{r, eval = FALSE}
# have to fix
```

Now implement routing for the rest of origins (can take several hours to run):
```{r}
n_origins <- nrow(origins_i_tract)

ttm_list <- vector("list", n_origins)

start.time <- Sys.time()

for(i in 1:n_origins){
  
  # Obtain the h3 polygons around the centroid of the tract at resolution 7
  h3_i <- geo_to_h3(c(origins_i_tract$lat[i], origins_i_tract$lon[i]), res = 7) |>
    k_ring(1)
  
  # Obtain the children of the res 7 polygons at resolution 13, whith are about 50 square meters in size
  h3_j <- purrr::map(h3_i,
                     .f = ~ h3_to_children(.x,
                                           res = 13)) |>
    unlist()
  
  # Obtain the coordinates of the res 13 polygons to use as destinations for origin i
  destinations_h3 <- h3_to_geo(h3_j)
  
  # Organize the data for the origins to match the format expected by {r5r} (id, lon, lat)
  destinations_j_h3 <- data.frame(id = h3_j, 
                                  lat = destinations_h3[,1],
                                  lon = destinations_h3[,2])
  
  # Routing for origin i
  ttm_list[[i]] <- travel_time_matrix(r5_cma,
                                      origins = origins_i_tract[i,],
                                      destinations = destinations_j_h3,
                                      mode = "WALK",
                                      departure_datetime = as.POSIXct(strptime("2021-04-05 08:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "EST5EDT")),
                                      max_walk_time = 15, # minutes
                                      max_trip_duration = 15)
}

ttm_i <- bind_rows(ttm_list)

end.time <- Sys.time()
time.taken <- end.time - start.time
time.taken
```

Swap the location of the to and from id columns (they're initially in the incorrect spots):
```{r}
ttm_i <- ttm_i |>
  rename(from_id = to_id,
         to_id = from_id)

# If running into issues with multipolygon generation later, ensure from_id are tract ids (only numbers), and to_id are h3 ids (numbers with a letter at the end)
```

Save the ttm file:
```{r}
# TTM
save(ttm_i, 
     file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data-raw/{params$city}_ttm_i.rda"),
     compress = "bzip2")

# save temporarily as the ttm_i files are large, but good to have in case walkshed (later chunks) have to be re-run.
```

Retrieve the h3 areas as multipolygons (can take several hours to run, but not as long as the initial routing):
```{r}
start.time <- Sys.time()

walksheds <- ttm_i |> 
  group_by(from_id) |>
  group_map(~ h3_set_to_multi_polygon(.x$to_id),
            .keep = TRUE)

end.time <- Sys.time()
time.taken <- end.time - start.time
time.taken
```

Obtain the GEOIDs of the walksheds:
```{r}
walkshed_IDs <- ttm_i |>
  group_by(from_id) |>
  summarize(from_id = first(from_id),
            .groups = "drop")
```

Convert to simple features identified by the origin:
```{r}
start.time <- Sys.time()

walksheds <- data.frame(GEOID = walkshed_IDs$from_id,
                         geometry = purrr::map_df(walksheds,
                            tibble::as_tibble)) |>
  st_as_sf(crs = 4326)

end.time <- Sys.time()
time.taken <- end.time - start.time
time.taken

# this chunk should take only a few seconds
```

Verify the catchments:
```{r, eval = FALSE}
test_unit = sample.int(nrow(walksheds), 1)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = tracts |>
            filter(GEOID == walksheds$GEOID[test_unit]),
          color = "black",
          fill= "lightgray") + 
  geom_sf(data = walksheds[test_unit,],
          color = "blue",
          fill = NA,
          linewidth = 1) #+
  #geom_sf(data = roads)
```

Save walksheds:
```{r save origin and destination files}
# Walksheds
save(walksheds, 
     file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data/{params$city}_walksheds.rda"),
     compress = "bzip2")
```

Plot a sample tract's walkshed:
```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = walksheds |>
            slice_sample(n = 1))
```

Calculate area of tract walksheds:
```{r}
walkshed_areas <- walksheds |>
  mutate(area = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)))
```


Create walksheds df with previous tracts df data and walkshed data:
```{r}
urban_tracts_df <- urban_tracts_df |>
  st_as_sf()

walkshed_areas <- walkshed_areas |>
  st_drop_geometry()

walksheds_df <- right_join(urban_tracts_df, walkshed_areas, by = "GEOID")
```

Rename walkshed area column:
```{r}
walksheds_df <- walksheds_df |>
  rename(WalkshedArea = area)
```

Plot the tracts and the walkshed area values:
```{r}
ggplot(walksheds_df, aes(fill = WalkshedArea)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Walkshed Size (m^2)")
```

Plot the tracts with RUCA value 1 (fully metropolitan/urban/non-commuting tracts) and their walkshed area values:
```{r}
RUCA_exclude <- c(2:6)

RUCA_1_tracts <- walksheds_df |>
  filter(!(PrimaryRUCA %in% RUCA_exclude))

ggplot(RUCA_1_tracts, aes(fill = WalkshedArea)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
labs(fill = "Walkshed Size (m^2)")
```

Calculate the new tract populations (based on the ones for which there are walksheds):
```{r}
total_walksheds_population <- sum(walksheds_df$PopulationCount)

total_walksheds_population

# note to self: record the value in the .xlsx sheet
```

Calculate the RUCA value 1 tract populations (based on the ones for which there are walksheds):
```{r}
RUCA_1_population <- sum(RUCA_1_tracts$PopulationCount)

RUCA_1_population

# note to self: record the value in the .xlsx sheet
```

Save the walksheds dataframe:
```{r}
# Origins
save(walksheds_df, 
     file = glue::glue(here::here(),
                       "/data-raw/intermediate-data-objects/{params$city}_walksheds_df.rda"),
     compress = "bzip2")
```

The chunks aren't all labeled yet! It's a work-in-progress. Everything should run without issues though.
